verdict.root_cause: Frontend's failures are entirely transport-level gRPC UNAVAILABLE connect errors (EHOSTUNREACH) to a single upstream endpoint 172.18.0.19:9555, with no connection ever established [tr_6ff7346a746a]. That endpoint is the ad service, whose log stream ends at 11:34:37 with an orderly JVM-shutdown-hook gRPC server stop after serving traffic cleanly, and emits nothing thereafter [tr_c85bcff4e31a]. The cause of the absence is in ad's change log: platform-automation flapped ad's image reference nine times in two hours, alternating set-to-hotfix-tag and revert-to-unset on an 11-13 minute cycle, with a set landing at 11:34:38, one second after the shutdown [tr_01c07e0c0e82]. The running artifact for ad is therefore not a correct, stable one, and during the gaps nothing listens on 9555, so callers get host-unreachable. Frontend is the reporter, not the fault: no changes [tr_a2f0a0ac1ded] and an error-span ratio below baseline with no step change at onset [tr_0f07ecb071ff].
verdict.reasoning: Frontend errors are connect-time failures to exactly one address and port, never a deadline, TLS, DNS or application error [tr_6ff7346a746a], which means the far end is absent rather than slow or rejecting. The far end stopped cleanly via a shutdown hook with no preceding warnings [tr_c85bcff4e31a], excluding crash, OOM, process_freeze (a frozen process does not log a graceful stop) and network_partition (a partitioned but running ad would still log and complain about its own reachability). The change history supplies the act: repeated image-reference set/revert churn by automation, the last set coinciding with the shutdown [tr_01c07e0c0e82]. Since every set names the same tag, this is not a defective new build but a workload left running the wrong (or no) artifact — the bad_deploy case. Frontend is excluded by its empty change log and sub-baseline error ratio [tr_a2f0a0ac1ded][tr_0f07ecb071ff]. Fix: stop the flap and pin ad to a known-good image so the workload comes back.
open_questions: The ad/172.18.0.19:9555 mapping is topology inference, not evidence; no result ties that IP to an ad pod [tr_6ff7346a746a].
The ad error-ratio query covered 2026-10-05, a day before the incident [tr_0361fa04f99c], so its 100%-error baseline and empty window may describe a different period.
Why platform-automation is flapping the image reference, and whether ad recovered on a later cycle, is unestablished; six of eight blast-radius services were never queried.

alternatives.root_cause: Ad is running but cut off at the network layer from its callers.
alternatives.why_not: A running-but-partitioned ad would keep logging and complain about reachability; its log instead ends at a clean shutdown with nothing after [tr_c85bcff4e31a].

alternatives.root_cause: The automation's reverts leave ad's image reference unset, and that wrong value is what stops the service existing.
alternatives.why_not: An image reference pointed at the wrong (or no) artifact is classed as bad_deploy by the taxonomy, even though it is configuration.

proposal.expected_effect: Ad's log stream, silent since the 11:34:37 shutdown-hook line, resumes with a gRPC server-started entry and AdService request lines; frontend's repeating 'UNAVAILABLE ... EHOSTUNREACH 172.18.0.19:9555' lines stop within ~60s of ad listening; sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="ad"}[5m])) returns non-zero samples instead of none.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if ad logs show a started server but frontend still emits EHOSTUNREACH to 172.18.0.19:9555 (the IP-to-ad mapping is topology inference, never confirmed). Also falsified if ad is stopped again within ~13 minutes: platform-automation flapped the image nine times on an 11-13 minute cycle, so the controller, not the artifact, is the fault, and stopping it is outside this system's reach. Third falsifier: no concrete prior tag exists (reverts return to unset) and the recreate fails to start.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this forces another restart on a service that may already be recovering on a later flap cycle, dropping its in-process cache and any in-flight ad requests. If the recorded prior reference is 'unset', the recreate may leave ad with no runnable image, turning an intermittent outage into a continuous one. It does not address the flapping automation, so relief may be temporary and may mask the real fault.
proposal.blast_radius: One service, ad. Frontend sees connections reset during the recreate; it is already failing every call to this endpoint, so the marginal harm is small. Checkout, product-catalog, recommendation, cart, product-reviews and frontend-proxy share the blast radius and would notice only if they also call ad.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and its proxy simultaneously affect the user-facing entry point and cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute this to, and the symmetric timing gives no clear signal between a frontend-side fault and a downstream dependency.
